# northflank_volume (Resource)

Manages a persistent volume in a Northflank project, and which services or jobs it is attached to.

**Destroying this resource deletes the volume and all data on it.** Consider `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }`. Changing `name`, `project_id`, `access_mode` or `storage_class` replaces the volume, which destroys its data too.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "northflank_project" "app" {
  name   = "My Application"
  region = "europe-west"
}

resource "northflank_deployment_service" "db" {
  project_id      = northflank_project.app.id
  name            = "Postgres"
  deployment_plan = "nf-compute-20"

  deployment = {
    external_image = {
      image_path = "postgres:16"
    }
  }
}

# A 10 GB volume holding the database files. Destroying this resource deletes
# the data, so guard it.
resource "northflank_volume" "db_data" {
  project_id   = northflank_project.app.id
  name         = "Postgres Data"
  storage_size = 10240

  mounts = [
    { container_path = "/var/lib/postgresql/data", volume_path = "pgdata" },
  ]

  attachments = [
    { id = northflank_deployment_service.db.id, type = "service" },
  ]

  lifecycle {
    prevent_destroy = true
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `mounts` (Attributes List) Where the volume is mounted in the containers it is attached to. The API does not report mounts back, so a change made outside Terraform is not detected, and an imported volume shows a difference until the next apply. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--mounts))
- `name` (String) Name of the volume, 3 to 39 characters. Changing this forces a new volume, since Northflank derives the `id` from it and cannot rename one.
- `project_id` (String) ID of the project the volume belongs to. Changing this forces a new volume.
- `storage_size` (Number) Size of the volume, in megabytes, such as `10240` for 10 GB. Which sizes are available depends on the storage class. Changes are applied in place; Northflank may refuse to shrink a volume.

### Optional

- `access_mode` (String) `ReadWriteOnce`, mountable by one instance at a time, or `ReadWriteMany`. Only `ReadWriteOnce` is generally available. Defaults to `ReadWriteOnce`. Changing this forces a new volume.
- `attachments` (Attributes Set) Services and jobs the volume is attached to. Attaching a volume to a service restarts it. With `ReadWriteOnce`, attach it to one workload with one instance. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--attachments))
- `storage_class` (String) Storage class, such as `nvme`. Northflank picks its default when this is not set. Changing this forces a new volume.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Creation time, in RFC 3339 format.
- `id` (String) Identifier of the volume, derived by Northflank from `name`.
- `status` (String) Status of the volume on the cluster, such as `BOUND`.
- `uid` (String) Permanent identifier of the volume. Unlike `id`, it never changes and is never reused.

<a id="nestedatt--mounts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `mounts`

Required:

- `container_path` (String) Path in the container to mount at, such as `/data`. Must be unique.

Optional:

- `volume_path` (String) Directory inside the volume to mount, instead of its root.


<a id="nestedatt--attachments"></a>
### Nested Schema for `attachments`

Required:

- `id` (String) ID of the service or job.
- `type` (String) `service` or `job`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Volumes are imported as <project_id>/<volume_id>. The API does not report
# mounts, so the first apply after an import sets them from configuration.
terraform import northflank_volume.db_data my-application/postgres-data
```
